risks: Reversing insertion order is not a load-bearing test for a tie. SQLite breaks an unordered tie by walking an index backwards, which reproduces reversed insertion - so a query with no tiebreaker looks correct. The first version of these tests did exactly that and passed against the unfixed code. Use a fixed non-monotone permutation (here [1,3,5,0,2,4]).

A docstring that asserts a performance property is not evidence of it. NEX-086 documented revoked_grants as bounded while its body read every grant row; NEX-087, NEX-088 and NEX-092 were the same defect in three layers. Suspect a docstring promising bounding above a select() with no where(...).

ci.yml declares concurrency group ci-<workflow>-<ref> with cancel-in-progress: true. A docs push while the product commit's runs are in flight cancels them, leaving the product commit with zero or cancelled check-runs. Read the product verdict before the docs push, or anchor it to a concluded docs head whose git diff against the product touches only docs/NEXUS.

decisions_this_run: The regression test observes work performed (_to_domain call count) rather than asserting on SQL text: a string assertion would pass for the wrong reason and pin the implementation, while the call count is the adapter's only row-to-domain path.
count_revoked became a count(*) aggregate so the port's 'without loading them' promise is actually kept; the WHERE clause is written once in the adapter, beside the one it must agree with.
is_active filtering stays in Python deliberately: it evaluates a clock against two nullable deadlines, which is real logic a SQL translation could drift from. is_revoked does not.
The docs push was deliberately delayed until the product commit's own runs concluded, because ci.yml cancels in-progress runs per ref.
run_summary: Run 93 continued: reconciled that the checkpoint's commit (3159555) was stale against the live head (bd736ce) with the run's two files uncommitted, and that the run's earlier status assumed all tiebreak tests were load-bearing when only 1 of 6 was. Root-caused that: reversed insertion is satisfied by SQLite's backwards index scan, so the test could not distinguish a fixed query from an unfixed one. Rebuilt all tiebreak tests on a non-monotone permutation (5 of 7 now fail without the fix), then extended the fix to list_pending_for_agent - the third query in the family, whose callers index [0] and so had which-approval-is-acted-on decided by an undefined order.
